content.description:
## Overview

A spreadsheet system for freelance rate projects. You keep entries in one place; the calculation sheets and summary views read from that single source, which keeps the numbers consistent as the file grows.

The structure is intentionally plain: named ranges and readable formulas rather than macros, so the file opens and behaves the same in Excel, Google Sheets and LibreOffice.

## Best for

- Owners and managers who track freelance rate projects in a spreadsheet rather than dedicated software

- Bookkeepers and analysts who need an auditable file rather than a black box

- Small teams standardising on one shared format

- Anyone replacing an inherited spreadsheet that has grown unmanageable

## Key features

- Single data-entry sheet feeding every downstream view

- Summary view with the headline figures for the period

- Month-over-month comparison with variance

- Category breakdown driven by the entries you record

- Charts that expand automatically as rows are added

- Named ranges throughout, so formulas stay readable

- Input validation on the fields that commonly get mistyped

- Print-ready summary layout sized to one page

- Settings sheet for labels, categories and rates

- No macros, so the file opens without security warnings

- Terminology matched to freelance rate projects

- Sample rows demonstrating the intended entry format

- **Step 3.** Read the summary and chart views — they recalculate from your entries.

content.description:
## Overview

Built around ride-sharing app, the kit separates tokens (colour, spacing, type) from components, which means a global restyle does not require touching every screen.

Spacing follows a single scale, which is what keeps screens looking related once other people start adding to them.

## Best for

- Product teams designing ride-sharing app

- Designers who need a defensible starting structure rather than a blank canvas

- Developers who want a documented spec to build against

- Founders preparing a prototype for user testing

## Key features

- Full screen flow for a ride-sharing app

- Shared design-token system (color, spacing, type)

- Component spec with states documented

- Light and dark variants

- Connected screen flow rather than isolated mockups

- Design tokens for colour, spacing and type scale

- Component set with states documented

- Light and dark treatments from one token source

- Consistent grid and spacing rhythm

- Form, list and navigation patterns

- Empty and error state designs

- Typography scale with defined usage

## What you'll get

The UI kit itself, supplied as Design tokens (JSON), Component spec, PNG screens, together with the licence tier you select at checkout and any future revisions to this product.

Package contents are listed under **What's included** on this page. Product updates are available from your DistroSource library at no additional cost.

## Compatibility

Any design tool supporting design tokens · Figma-compatible structure

## Requirements

- A design tool that supports components and shared styles

## How to use it

- **Step 1.** Open the kit and review the token definitions first.

- **Step 2.** Adjust colour, type and spacing tokens to your brand.

- **Step 3.** Assemble new screens from the existing components.

- **Step 4.** Share the component spec with developers for handoff.

## Customization

- Retheme every screen by editing the token set

- Extend the component library following the documented conventions

- Adjust the type scale without breaking layout rhythm

- Add screens using the existing grid and spacing rules

## Licence

- **Personal** — for your own private, non-commercial projects. Not for client work or anything that generates revenue.

- **Commercial** — for one commercial project or one client project. A separate licence is needed for each additional project.

- **Agency** — for multiple client projects, up to the limits stated on this page and recorded on your order.

No tier permits reselling or redistributing the files themselves, and none grants resale of source files.

content.description:
## Overview

A spreadsheet system for rental property projects. You keep entries in one place; the calculation sheets and summary views read from that single source, which keeps the numbers consistent as the file grows.

The structure is intentionally plain: named ranges and readable formulas rather than macros, so the file opens and behaves the same in Excel, Google Sheets and LibreOffice.

## Best for

- Owners and managers who track rental property projects in a spreadsheet rather than dedicated software

- Bookkeepers and analysts who need an auditable file rather than a black box

- Small teams standardising on one shared format

- Anyone replacing an inherited spreadsheet that has grown unmanageable

## Key features

- Pre-built categories and structure

- Works in Excel and Google Sheets

- Set up specifically as a rental property tracker

- Clean, color-coded layout

- Single data-entry sheet feeding every downstream view

- Summary view with the headline figures for the period

- Month-over-month comparison with variance

- Category breakdown driven by the entries you record

- Charts that expand automatically as rows are added

- Named ranges throughout, so formulas stay readable

- Input validation on the fields that commonly get mistyped

- Print-ready summary layout sized to one page
